capture.final_message:
Use set extensionality and reduce both equalities to elementwise logic.

- For `sInter {s} = s`, show that `x` belongs to the intersection exactly when it belongs to every set in the singleton family, hence exactly when `x ∈ s`.
- For distributivity, reduce membership to
  \[
  x\in s\land(\forall i,\ x\in t_i)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \forall i,\ x\in s\land x\in t_i.
  \]
  The forward direction is immediate. For the reverse direction, choose one index using `[Nonempty ι]` to recover `x ∈ s`, while the indexed hypotheses directly give every `x ∈ t i`.

The nonemptiness assumption is essential: for an empty index type, the right-hand intersection is universal while the left-hand side remains `s`.
